sections.title: What Is Inventory Management?
sections.text:
7.1 What Is Inventory Management?
Inventory management manages and records all physical movements of goods in the
system. It also has capabilities to manage the quantities of physical stocks in all plants
in the enterprise. Integration with financial accounting means that the financial
impacts to general ledgers are posted immediately upon recording the goods move-
ment in the SAP S/4HANA system. Inventory management has extensive reporting
capabilities so that stock balances and goods movements can be made visible to the
enterprise, facilitating end-to-end process harmonization.
Inventory management in the SAP S/4HANA system has the following solution capa-
bilities:
 Goods receipt
 Goods issue
 Stock transfers
 Transfer postings
 Basic warehouse management
 Basic shipping
For the purposes of this book, we’ll focus on the solution capabilities of inventory man-
agement that impact SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and Procurement business processes,
which are goods receipt, goods issue, stock transfers, and transfer postings.
The inventory management data model for stocks in prior versions of SAP ERP was
quite complex. Each material document, which is the system record for goods

movements, was represented in the system in two tables: a header record containing
date, time, and user information, and one or more line items containing information
about the purpose of the movement, material, quantities, units of measure, and so on.
Using these tables involved joining the two to obtain a unified dataset for the applica-
tion or query at hand. Figure 7.2 shows both the SAP Business Suite powered by SAP
HANA and the SAP S/4HANA inventory management data models in more detail.

The material master had a key role in inventory management as well. Two tables used

used to hold stock quantities and values at the plant and storage-location-data levels,
respectively. This meant that inserts into the database for goods movements required
locking the material master at the respective level being transacted. This was quite

In addition, other tables were used to store quantities and values that were specific to
the kind of stock being processed. These tables needed to be updated during goods
movement postings as well, which further complicated the updates. These included
tables MCHB (Stocks at Batch Level), MKOL (Special Stocks from Supplier), and many others.
Several aggregate tables were also present in the data model for use in reporting appli-
cations. These aggregate tables summarized the stock movement and balance data into
time-phased buckets. Finally, historical stock balance tables were also built into the
data model for use in reporting and costing.
The inventory management data model has been completely rearchitected for the SAP
HANA in-memory platform. The material document has been reduced to one table,
table MATDOC, which contains header and line-item data for goods movements. The
stock quantity and amount fields, which were previously stored in the hybrid tables,
have been eliminated. The stock aggregate and historical stock tables have also been
eliminated.
This simplification reduces the total data footprint required to maintain inventory
management data and therefore increases the transactional throughput of the system
because transactions now don’t need to update nearly as many tables as before. It also
means that only main tables are needed; redundancy in the database is eliminated. The
master data is now clearly separated from the transactional data in the data model. Less
data means a smaller memory footprint, increasing throughput.
All stock calculations now harness the power of the SAP S/4HANA database and read
table MATDOC directly. This allows stock balances, both current and historical, to be calcu-
lated in real time, without the need for aggregate tables. Analytics can now be calcu-
lated in real time and allow analysis at the most granular level. This capability enables
inventory managers to react to operational situations and eliminate bottlenecks in
material flow through the enterprise.
This architecture also eliminates the need for material master locking during INSERT
operations on the database, thus improving transactional throughput by a factor of 10
to 25 times. Analytics now run natively and avoid the overhead involved in JOIN opera-
tions on the underlying data tables.
Twenty-one tables were eliminated in the new inventory management data model, and
stock aggregate columns in eight additional tables were removed as well.
Material valuation data was previously housed in the accounting tables of the material
master. Now the material ledger is required in SAP S/4HANA and is used to house mate-
rial valuation data. This allows inventory valuation in multiple currencies to be main-
tained consistently. The valuation tables in the classic SAP ERP data model (table MBEW
and others) have been eliminated from the data model. Note that SAP does provide CDS

7.2 Stock Management in SAP S/4HANA
The identification, tracking, and management of physical stocks is the core purpose of
inventory management. The functions of the system allow all goods movements
affecting physical stocks to be recorded in real time. This allows stock balances to be
instantly obtained, both for the present and for any point in the past. If the material
type assigned to the material requires financial valuation, then the appropriate finan-
cial documents are immediately posted in the system when the goods movements are
recorded.
It is useful to consider stock management as a collection of multiple data elements that
relate to one another. Each data element reflects an individual aspect of the stock—for
example, the condition, location, and physical and logistical attributes of the stock
itself:
 Material identification
 Location of the stock
 Usability of the stock
 Ownership of the stock
 Batch identification
 Serial number identification

sections.title: Material Identification
sections.text:
7.2.1 Material Identification
Each item in stock is identified with a material number. This material number rep-
resents stocks that are distinct from another—for instance, different raw materials
used in a production process. Each material is represented in the system with a unique
material number, which can be up to 40 characters in length. Each material has a mate-
rial type attribute, which defines control features for a grouping of materials.

sections.title: Location of the Stock
sections.text:
7.2.2 Location of the Stock
The location information in inventory management consists of two attributes:
 Plant, the physical location where logistics activities in support of the enterprise are
transacted
 Storage location, a subset of a plant used for stock management purposes

7 Inventory Management
242
All stock managed in an enterprise must be assigned to a plant. The plant provides the
linkage to financial accounting via the company code assigned to that plant.
If the stock is managed in a facility that the enterprise owns or controls, then the stock
is assigned to a storage location upon receipt. However, there are other types of stocks
in an enterprise that do not require a storage location. A good example of this is stock
that is being transferred between two facilities. If goods being transferred have been
issued from the supplying plant but haven’t yet arrived in the receiving plant, then the
stock in SAP S/4HANA is designated as in transit to the receiving plant and doesn’t
show a storage location. A storage location must be specified upon goods receipt into
stock at the receiving plant.

sections.title: Usability of the Stock
sections.text:
7.2.3 Usability of the Stock
Stock type is the term used in SAP to designate the disposition or usability of the stock
for materials planning and execution purposes. There are four main stock types sup-
ported in SAP S/4HANA:
 Unrestricted use
The unrestricted use stock type is used to designate inventory quantities that are free
to be considered for materials planning or execution purposes, such as deliveries to
customers or consumption for production. Unrestricted use stocks can also be freely
transferred between plants and storage locations.
 Quality inspection
The quality inspection stock type is used for identifying quantities of goods that are
currently undergoing processing by the quality department. Quality inspection
stocks are considered available by materials planning. However, these stocks can’t
be shipped to a customer or consumed internally until a decision has been made
regarding their usability. They can be transferred between storage locations in a
plant but can’t be transferred between plants.
Quality inspection stocks may be under the control of quality management. If qual-
ity management is active for that material in that plant, then its processes control
the postings of material into and out of the quality inspection stock type. If quality
management isn’t active for that material in that plant, then transfer postings are
used to post stocks out of quality inspection stock into other stock types.
 Blocked
The blocked stock type is used when a material becomes unusable for planning and
execution purposes, for example, if stocks are damaged in storage. Blocked stocks
generally aren’t considered during materials planning. Blocked stocks can’t be used
for fulfilling customer or production demands. Blocked stocks can be transferred
between storage locations within a plant.
Note that unrestricted use, quality inspection, and blocked stocks are considered
valuated stocks if the stock type assigned to the material is valuated in the valuation
area assigned to the plant.
© 

243
7.2 Stock Management in SAP S/4HANA
 Customer returns
The customer returns stock type is a less commonly used stock type. It can be used to
manage goods that have been delivered back into a storage location from a customer
and for which a decision hasn’t yet been made as to whether the goods will be accepted
back into stock. Customer returns stock is always nonvaluated stock. Once a decision
is made to accept the goods, a transfer posting from customer returns to either unre-
stricted use, quality inspection, or blocked stock is made. This transfer posting posts
the quantities into valuated stock and creates an accounting document.

sections.title: Ownership of the Stock
sections.text:
7.2.4 Ownership of the Stock
Most stocks in an SAP S/4HANA system are owned by the enterprise and are reflected
in the appropriate stock accounts in financial accounting. However, it is possible to rep-
resent stocks that are owned by an external party in the system. Special stock indica-
tors are used to represent a variety of ownership scenarios in inventory management.
Each special stock has a unique one-letter identifier in the database.
The following are examples of special stocks that are owned by the enterprise and
physically stored at an external location:
 Component stocks provided to supplier for subcontracting (special stock O)
 Finished goods consigned to a customer (special stock W)
 Returnable transport packaging at customer (special stock V)
Note that these special stocks can be in either unrestricted use or quality inspection
stock types.
The following are examples of special stocks owned by an external party and physically
stored in a plant and storage location:
 Supplier consignment stock (special stock K)
 Supplier-owned returnable transport packaging (special stock M)

sections.title: Batch Identification
sections.text:
7.2.5 Batch Identification
Many industries, such as food or pharmaceuticals, require stock management based on
the attributes of a manufacturing lot of a material. SAP S/4HANA provides batch man-
agement to fill these needs. A batch is defined as a subset of a material with a set of
attributes that have common values.
If you need a material to be batch-managed in the SAP S/4HANA system, set the batch
management indicator on a material master view at the plant level, such as the pur-
chasing view.
A batch can contain one or more characteristics, which are equivalent to the attributes
being measured. Each characteristic in a batch can contain one or more values that

7 Inventory Management
244
differentiate one batch from another for that material. Typically, the characteristic val-
ues are recorded upon the initial goods receipt of a batch-managed material from pro-
duction or procurement.
All goods movements for batch-managed materials must identify the unique batch of
the material being transacted.
Note that it is very difficult to change the batch management indicator on a material
once material movements have been recorded in the system. Therefore, consider care-
fully before setting the batch management indicator on the material master.

sections.title: Serial Number Identification
sections.text:
7.2.6 Serial Number Identification
Some industries need to identify individual units of a material—for example, con-
sumer electronics or medical devices, for which it is important to track units for cus-
tomer servicing and warranty purposes. Serial number management is used in SAP
S/4HANA to meet these requirements.
Making a material relevant for serialization involves the assignment of a serial number
profile in the storage view of the material master. The serial number profile is set up in
system configuration and designates the types of business transactions for which
serial numbers need to be recorded.
If serialization is active for inventory management for a material in a plant, then serial
numbers must be recorded for each unit of material in a goods movement.

sections.title: Goods Movements
sections.text:
7.3 Goods Movements
Goods movements are transactions in SAP S/4HANA that result in a change in stock.
There are four main types of goods movements:
 Goods receipts
These are goods movements that result in an increase in quantities of stock.
 Goods issues
These are goods movements that result in a decrease in quantities of stock.
 Stock transfers
These are goods movements that result in quantities of stock moving between two
logistics organizational elements. For instance, you can transfer stock between two
plants in an enterprise or between two storage locations in a plant.
 Transfer postings
These are goods movements that result in a change in identity, disposition, or own-
ership of a material. Transfer postings can be done in conjunction with stock trans-
fers in some cases.
© 

245
7.3 Goods Movements
Each goods movement in the SAP S/4HANA system is recorded as a material docu-
ment. A material document contains information on the type of goods movement, the
date and time of posting, the identifier of the user that created the goods movement,
the materials transacted, quantities and units of measure, and associated details. The
details are recorded in table MATDOC in SAP S/4HANA.
Many goods movements reference other SAP S/4HANA documents. For instance, a
goods receipt from a supplier can reference a purchasing document and line item. This
information is recorded in the material document as well.
Each material document line item contains a movement type code. The movement
type in the SAP S/4HANA system is represented by a three-character code that identi-
fies the type of goods movement to be recorded (goods receipt, goods issue, transfer
posting). Movement types play an important control function in determining what
data is required to successfully post the goods movement and to pass information into
other system components, such as financial accounting. Special stock indicators are
used for some movement types depending on the situation.
Movement types are paired with a reversal movement type. These reversal movement
types are used to undo a movement already posted in the system. It is typical practice
to have the reversal movement type be one more than the movement type number.
For example, the reversal movement type for a goods receipt for a purchase order (101)
is 102.
Examples of movement types important for SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and Procurement
include the following:
 101: Goods Receipt for a Purchasing Document
 543 O: Goods Issue from Component Stock Provided to Supplier

sections.title: Goods Receipts
sections.text:
7.3.1 Goods Receipts
Goods receipts are goods movements that result in an increase in stock. They are
important goods movements for SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and Procurement as they
form an important process link between purchasing and financial accounting. Goods
receipts usually reference other SAP S/4HANA documents, such as purchase orders or
inbound deliveries. This streamlines the entry of the goods receipt data, much of which
can be copied directly from the reference document. However, there are types of goods
receipts that can be entered without any reference, such as when initial stocks are
entered into the system at startup.
Goods receipts can be entered into the SAP S/4HANA system in two ways: a material
document can be posted directly in the system using the Post Goods Movement app or,
if the supplier of the goods transmits an advance shipping notification (ASN) to you,
you can then convert this communication into an inbound delivery document in SAP
S/4HANA. Inbound delivery documents can be used when available to plan inbound

7 Inventory Management
246
receipts with much more precision in materials planning. This is due to the shipped
quantities and delivery dates being much firmer than at the time of purchase order
entry or order acknowledgement.
The inbound delivery can be created in the SAP S/4HANA system with reference to one
or more purchasing documents. As an alternative, these documents can also be created
via the receipt of an advance shipping notification from the supplier of the goods prior
to the actual receipt. EDI or SAP Business Network are often utilized by companies to
transmit ASNs to an SAP S/4HANA system. Inbound deliveries allow for more precise
planning of the inbound movements and provide up-to-date firm supply data to mate-
rials planning.
The confirmation control key entered on the purchasing document line item controls
the method by which a goods receipt is posted. If the confirmation control key allows
inbound deliveries, then that document must be referenced to receive the goods. Oth-
erwise, the purchase order or scheduling agreement line item can be referenced
directly at goods receipt.
Here are some examples of goods receipts movement types used in the system:
 Movement types for goods receipts with reference to documents
– 101: Goods Receipt with reference to Purchase Order or Production Order
 Movement types for goods receipts without reference
– 561: Initial Stock Entry for Unrestricted Use Stock
– 563: Initial Stock Entry for Quality Inspection Stock
– 565: Initial Stock Entry for Blocked Stock
Goods receipts can be posted using SAP Fiori apps that post goods movements directly
into inventory management. Some goods receipts also can be posted using apps that
integrate with shipping documents, such as inbound deliveries. Both types of goods
receipts are described in the following sections.
Posting Goods Receipts
There are a variety of SAP Fiori apps for inventory management that can be used to
record the arrival of goods at your facility. These apps are described in more detail in
the sections ahead.
The following SAP Fiori apps are available in SAP S/4HANA for processing goods
receipts:
 Post Goods Receipt for Purchasing Document
 Post Goods Receipt without Reference
 Manage Stock
 Post Subsequent Adjustment
 Material Documents Overview

247
7.3 Goods Movements
In addition, the following SAP GUI for HTML apps are also available for processing
goods receipts:
 Post Goods Movement
 Output Material Documents
Post Goods Receipt for Purchasing Document
The Post Goods Receipt for Purchasing Document app is used to record the physical
receipt of goods into a facility. This app requires the receipt of these goods to be made
with reference to an existing purchasing document, such as a purchase order or sched-
uling agreement. It is vital that goods receipts reference the correct purchasing docu-
ments used to order them for the procure-to-pay business process to work efficiently.
The Post Goods Receipt for Purchasing Document app (see Figure 7.3) lets you do the
following:
 Post the receipt of goods with reference to a purchasing document that contains
order items for stock material (procurement for stock).
 Post the receipt of goods with reference to a purchasing document that contains
order items with single or multiple account assignments (procurement for direct
consumption).
 Post the receipt of goods into supplier consignment stock.
 Receipt of goods received from subcontractors.
 Post the receipt of goods into goods receipt blocked stock, which will be released
after evaluation.
 Post the receipt of shelf life–managed materials into stock.
 Post the receipt into stock of items that have been issued from stock transport pur-
chase orders.
 Assign batches during goods receipt processing for those materials that require them.
 Assign serial numbers during goods receipt processing for those materials that
require them.
 Use predefined output forms in output management for material documents, which
can be copied and changed according to your requirements.
This app cannot process purchasing document items which fulfill at least one of the fol-
lowing conditions:
 The Delivery Completed line-item indicator is set.
 The line item contains an account assignment category that is not supported by the app.
 Receipts for scheduling agreements for stock transport.
If all items of a purchasing document fulfill at least one of these conditions, the pur-
chasing document is not able to be processed in this app. Use the Post Goods Move-
ment app as an alternative.

The Manage Stock app (see Figure 7.5) can perform the following types of goods move-
ments in the SAP S/4HANA system:
 Initial entry of stock balances for unrestricted use, quality inspection or blocked
stocks.
 Scrapping of material for unrestricted use, quality inspection or blocked stocks.

You will be asked to enter a material and plant. The screen in Figure 7.5 will be shown.
Click the up arrow next to the storage location and stock type that you would like to
perform transactions on. The Manage Stock processing dialog box (see Figure 7.6) is

7.3 Goods Movements
The Manage Stock app supports movement-type-dependent reason codes. Reason
codes let you add a short explanation for the underlying purpose of a specific goods
movement, such as poor quality. You can also enter free texts for the document header
or for an individual line item. The Manage Stock app lets you check the range of cover-
age based on the consumption of unrestricted stock in the last 30 days.
If you notice that you’ve made an error in posting goods movements, you can correct
the error by reversing the material document and posting the goods movements again.
To reverse the material document, use the Material Documents Overview app. The
Manage Stock app is assigned to the inventory manager standard authorization role.
Post Subsequent Adjustment
The Post Subsequent Adjustment app (see Figure 7.7) is used to make correction entries
in stocks consumed during a subcontracting process. When a goods receipt for a sub-
contracted item is posted, goods issues are done for the components sent to the sup-
plier, based on the bill of material maintained in the purchasing document line item.
Sometimes, suppliers consume more or less of a component than planned. This app
allows component corrections, both over- and underconsumptions, to be made after
the original goods receipt is posted.
This app requires the following:
 The referenced purchasing document line item must have a subcontracting item
category.
 A goods receipt must have already been posted for the selected line item.

Post Goods Movement
The Post Goods Movement app (see Figure 7.9) is used to perform goods movements,
including goods receipts, in the SAP S/4HANA system. It can also be used to review a
specific material document and its associated documents. This app is used when the
simplified goods receipt SAP Fiori apps do not support all aspects of the type of goods
receipts needed for your enterprise—for example, if custom goods receipt movement
types are used.
The Post Goods Movement app runs directly on the backend SAP S/4HANA system and
is functionally equivalent to the classic SAP ERP Transaction MIGO. The Post Goods
Movement app is assigned to the inventory manager and warehouse clerk standard
authorization roles.
Figure 7.9 Post Goods Movement App
Output Material Documents
The Output Material Documents app (see Figure 7.10) is used to create printouts, goods
receipt labels, and other types of messages from the inventory management compo-
nent.
The Output Material Documents app runs directly on the backend SAP S/4HANA sys-
tem and is functionally equivalent to the classic SAP ERP Transaction MB90. The Out-
put Material Documents app is assigned to the inventory manager and warehouse
clerk standard authorization roles.

Processing Goods Receipts via Inbound Deliveries
There are a variety of apps that can be used to record the arrival of goods at your facility
if your supplier transmits details to you via an advance shipment notification. These
apps are described in more detail in the following sections.
The Post Goods Receipt for Inbound Delivery app is available in SAP S/4HANA for pro-
cessing goods receipts that reference inbound deliveries. In addition, the following SAP
GUI for HTML apps are also available:
 Inbound Deliveries for Purchase Orders
 Create Inbound Delivery
 Change Inbound Delivery
 Display Inbound Delivery
 My Inbound Delivery Monitor

The Post Goods Receipt for Inbound Delivery app (see Figure 7.11) enables a user to
record goods receipts with reference to an inbound delivery document. The app dis-
plays a selection of inbound deliveries from the supplier that can be posted.
Note that if an inbound delivery is required for the purchasing document, this app
must be used to post the receipt of the goods. This requirement is controlled via the
confirmation control key on the purchasing document line item.
This app can be used to do the following:

7.3.2 Goods Issues
Goods issues are classified as goods movements that result in a decrease in stock quan-
tities. Goods issues can be planned in the SAP S/4HANA system or can be executed
without preplanning.
Planned goods issues are issued with reference to an existing document, such as an
outbound delivery for a customer order or a reservation for production materials.
Those customers requiring shipping integration with their goods issue processes will
generally reference outbound delivery documents created by the warehouse.
Unplanned goods issues are issued without any reference. Examples include scrapping
of defective material or issuing samples from stock.
Here are the movement types for goods issues with and without reference documents:
 Movement types for goods issues with reference to documents
– 261: Goods Issue to Production Order
– 601: Goods Issue to Outbound Delivery to Customer
– 641: Goods Issue to In-Transit Stock between Plants in Same Company Code
– 643: Goods Issue to In-Transit Stock between Plants in Differing Company Codes
 Movement types for goods issues without reference
– 201: Goods Issue to Cost Center
– 333: Goods Issue to Sampling from Unrestricted Use Stock
– 551: Goods Issue to Scrap from Unrestricted Use Stock

7.3.3 Stock Transfers
Stock transfers are goods movements in inventory management that result in a
change in physical or logical location for the goods being transacted. Stock transfers
can be done within a plant or between two distinct plants. There are three types of stock
transfers:
 From one storage location to another storage location within a plant
 From one plant to another plant within a company code
 From one plant to another plant, where the plants are in different company codes
Stock transfers can take place using one-step or two-step processes. In one-step stock
transfers, the material moves from the issuing plant and storage location to the receiv-
ing plant and storage location immediately upon posting. One-step stock transfers are
typically used when goods movements are performed in the system after the physical
transfer takes place or when the transit time between the two storage locations is min-
imal. The following movement types are used for one-step stock transfers:
 301: Plant to Plant
 311: Storage Location to Storage Location
Two-step stock transfers are used to separately record the goods issue from the issuing
plant and storage location from the goods receipt into the receiving plant and storage
location. This two-step process has the benefit of providing visibility into in-transit
stock quantities between the two locations. The following movement types are used
for two-step stock transfers:
 303: Plant to Plant—Goods Issue from Shipping Plant/Storage Location
 305: Plant to Plant—Goods Receipt in Receiving Plant/Storage Location
 313: Storage Location to Storage Location—Goods Issue from Shipping Storage Loca-
tion
 315: Storage Location to Storage location – Goods Receipt in Receiving Storage Loca-
tion
Note that these movement types can only be used with unrestricted use stock.
Simple movements of stock can be recorded in the SAP S/4HANA system with just a
material document. The following apps can be used to perform stock transfers using
inventory management goods movements:
 Transfer Stock—In-Plant
 Transfer Stock—Cross-Plant
We’ll describe these apps in the following sections. Following their discussion, we’ll
dive into the methods by which these are done, via stock transport orders and in-transit
stock reporting.

7.3 Goods Movements
Stock Transport
While using inventory management goods movement to process material transfers is
a simple method, most companies require more precise tracking of goods movements
in materials planning, purchasing, and the warehouse. SAP offers the use of stock trans-
port orders (STOs) to facilitate these detailed requirements.
A stock transport order is a kind of purchase order. A stock transport order uses a sup-
plying plant code in lieu of a supplier in the header of the purchase order. You can think
of a stock transport order as a purchase from an internal supplier to your company
group instead of an external supplier. There are two kinds of stock transport orders:
 Intracompany stock transport orders
The supplying and receiving plants belong to the same company code.
 Intercompany stock transport order
The supplying and receiving plants belong to different company codes.
Stock transport orders have the following advantages over inventory management
stock transfer movements:
 The goods receipt can be planned in the receiving plant.
 A separate freight supplier can be entered in the order and freight bills matched to
these freight suppliers.
 Delivery costs can be captured and billed.
 Materials planning can see the planned supply in the receiving plant, and the
demand in the issuing plant once the stock transport order is created.
 Outbound deliveries are used to manage the outbound process in the warehouse,
similar to the process used to deliver goods to the customer.
There are three process variations, which we’ll discuss in the following sections, for the
stock transfer process using stock transport orders:
 Stock transport order without delivery
 Stock transport order with delivery using shipping
 Stock transport order with delivery and billing document
The process variation used depends on your business requirements for tracing the
logistics flow from planning, shipping, in-transit stock, and receiving the goods.
Stock Transport Order without Delivery
The stock transport order without delivery process variant uses only stock transport
purchase orders to manage the process. No logistics documents are utilized. The pur-
chase order type in the standard system is UB, and the item category on each line item
is U. The goods movements are valuated at the price of the material in the issuing plant.

7 Inventory Management
268
The Post Goods Movement app can be used to post goods movements with reference
to the stock transport order. The movement types are 351 for the goods issue in the
issuing plant and 101 for the goods receipt in the receiving plant. Note that the stock
transport order without delivery process can only be done with a two-step process.
All goods movements are recorded in the purchase order history of the stock transport
order. Both the intracompany and intercompany variants are supported.
The prerequisites for the stock transport order without delivery process variant are as
follows:
 Material masters for the goods being transferred are set up in both plants
 A ship-to customer master is set up that represents the receiving plant
The steps in the stock transport order without delivery process flow are as follows:
1. Stock transport requisition is created manually or via materials planning (optional)
2. Stock transport order is created manually, or by converting stock transport requisi-
tions
3. A goods issue with reference to the stock transport order is done in the issuing plant,
which decrements the material and moves it into in-transit stock into the issuing
plant
4. In-transit stock is monitored
5. A goods receipt with reference to the stock transport order is done in the receiving
plant
Stock Transport Order with Delivery via Shipping
The stock transport order with delivery via shipping process variant uses outbound
deliveries in addition to stock transport purchase orders to manage the process. The pur-
chase order type in the standard system is UB, and the item category on each line item is
U. The goods movements are valuated at the price of the material in the issuing plant.
This process variant supports both one-step and two-step movements of material.
Stock transport orders with deliveries is the most common process used to execute
intracompany stock transport orders as it has integration with the logistics depart-
ment and does not require billing documents to be exchanged between the plants.
Outbound deliveries are used to manage the outbound process in the warehouse, sim-
ilar to the process used in sales to deliver goods to customers.
All goods movements are posted with reference to the outbound delivery created with
reference to the stock transport order. The movement type for the goods issue in the
issuing plant is 647 for the one-step process and movement type 641 for the two-step
process. The movement type for the goods receipt in the receiving plant is 101 for the
two-step process. Note that no goods receipt is necessary in the one-step process as the
goods move into the unrestricted stock of the receiving plant immediately upon goods
issue from the issuing plant.
© 

269
7.3 Goods Movements
All goods movements are recorded in the purchase order history of the stock transport
order. Both the intracompany and intercompany variants are supported.
The prerequisites for the stock transport order with delivery process variant are as fol-
lows:
 Material masters for the goods being transferred are set up in both plants
 A supplier master is set up that represents the issuing plant
 A ship-to customer master is set up that represents the receiving plant
The steps in the stock transport order with delivery (one step) process flow are as
follows:
1. Stock transport requisition is created manually or via materials planning (optional).
2. Stock transport order is created manually, or by converting stock transport requisi-
tions.
3. A replenishment outbound delivery (document type NL) is created with reference to
the stock transport order to manage the shipping activities.
4. The goods are picked from the warehouse and staged for delivery.
5. A goods issue with reference to the replenishment outbound delivery is done in the
issuing plant, which decrements the material.
6. A goods receipt in the receiving plant is automatically done upon successful posting
of the goods issue.
The steps in the stock transport order with delivery (two-step) process flow are as fol-
lows:
1. Stock transport requisition is created manually or via materials planning (optional).
2. Stock transport purchase order is created manually or by converting stock transport
requisitions into STOs.
3. A replenishment outbound delivery (document type NL) is created with reference to
the stock transport order to manage the shipping activities.
4. The goods are picked from the warehouse and staged for delivery.
5. A goods issue with reference to the replenishment outbound delivery is done in the
issuing plant, which decrements the material stocks and moves them into in-transit
stock into the issuing plant.
6. In-transit stock is monitored.
7. A goods receipt with reference to the replenishment outbound delivery is done in
the receiving plant upon receipt of the goods.
Stock Transport Order with Delivery and Billing Document
The stock transport order with delivery and billing document process variant uses out-
bound deliveries in addition to stock transport orders to manage the process. The pur-
chase order type in the standard system is NB, and the item category on each line item

7 Inventory Management
270
is blank. While this is similar to a purchase order to an external supplier, the supplier on
an intercompany STO must be linked to the issuing plant code in the business partner
master data.
The goods movements are valuated at the price of the material in the issuing plant
which is maintained in purchasing pricing condition records. This process variant sup-
ports both one-step and two-step movements of material.
This is the most common scenario to process intercompany stock transport orders as
they require integration with the logistics department and require billing documents
to be exchanged between the two companies.
Outbound deliveries are used to manage the outbound process in the warehouse, sim-
ilar to the process used by sales to deliver goods to customers.
All goods movements are posted with reference to the outbound delivery created from
the stock transport order. The movement type for the goods issue in the issuing plant
is 641. The movement type for the goods receipt in the receiving plant is 101. All goods
movements are recorded in the purchase order history of the stock transport order.
The prerequisites for the stock transport order with delivery and billing document pro-
cess variant are as follows:
 Material masters are set up in both plants
 Supplier master is set up that represents the issuing plant
 Ship-to customer master is set up that represents the receiving plant
 Purchasing pricing condition records exist for pricing the material in the stock
transport order
 Billing condition records exist for pricing the material in the intercompany billing
document
The steps in the stock transport order with delivery two-step process flow are as fol-
lows:
1. A stock transport requisition is created manually or via materials planning
(optional).
2. A stock transport order is created manually, or by converting stock transport requi-
sitions.
3. A replenishment outbound delivery (document type NLCC) is created with reference
to the stock transport order to manage the outbound shipping activities.
4. The goods are picked from the warehouse and staged for delivery.
5. A goods issue with reference to the replenishment outbound delivery is done in the
issuing plant, which decrements the material stocks and transfers them into cross-
company in-transit stock into the receiving plant.
6. A billing document for the shipped goods is produced and presented to the receiv-
ing company code.
© 

271
7.3 Goods Movements
7. Cross company in-transit stock is monitored.
8. A goods receipt with reference to the replenishment outbound delivery is done in
the receiving plant upon receipt of the goods.
9. A vendor invoice is created with reference to the billing document in the receiving
company code.
In-Transit Stock Reporting
It’s important to monitor the status of in-transit stocks in the system, especially those
that involve a two-step process. This will ensure that all physical stock transfers are
posted in a timely manner and that up-to-date stock information is available for mate-
rials planning.
SAP S/4HANA provides the following apps to obtain reports for in-process stock trans-
fers:
 Display Stock in Transit
 Stock in Transit on Key Date
 Overdue Materials—Stock in Transit
We’ll describe these apps in the following sections.
Display Stock in Transit
The Display Stock in Transit app (see Figure 7.26) is used to show all stocks that have
been issued from one plant and are currently in transit to another plant. It also shows
stock transport purchase order references and the value of the goods transferred.
Figure 7.26 Display Stock in Transit App

272
The Display Stock in Transit app runs directly on the backend SAP S/4HANA system
and is functionally equivalent to the classic SAP ERP Transaction MB5T. The Display

The Stock in Transit on Key Date app (see Figure 7.27) is used to show all stocks that
have been issued from one plant and are currently in transit to another plant on a spec-
ified key date. It also shows stock transport order references and the value of the goods
in transit.
Figure 7.27 Stock in Transit on Key Date App

Overdue Materials—Stock in Transit
The Overdue Materials—Stock in Transit app (see Figure 7.28) provides information on
materials for which a stock transport order has been created and issued, but which have
not been received to date. You can identify these materials to complete the stock trans-

Use the Overdue Materials—Stock in Transit app to do the following:

plant.

hasn’t yet been completed, has been completed, or both.

then choosing one of the following apps: Post Goods Receipt for Purchasing Docu-

stock quantity of the selected reporting date multiplied by the current material
price.

sections.title: Transfer Postings
sections.text:
7.3.4 Transfer Postings
Transfer postings are goods movements that result in a change in identity, usability, or
ownership for a quantity of stock. Typically, the stock doesn’t physically move in the
system during a transfer posting. However, it is possible to combine some types of
transfer postings with changes in location as well.
The Transfer Stock—In-Plant app is used to post transfer postings in the SAP S/4HANA
system. The Post Goods Movements app also can be utilized to create transfer posting
goods movements. Descriptions of these apps can be found in Section 7.3.3.
Let’s take a closer look at the types of transfer postings, as follows:
 Stock identity
Transfer postings that result in a change in stock identity involve a change in mate-
rial. Note that a material can only to transferred to the stock of another material if
both materials share the same base unit of measure. If a material is batch-managed
in the SAP S/4HANA system, a change in batch identity can also be posted. Both the
material and batch can be changed at the same time. The 309 movement type is

7 Inventory Management
274
used to change material or batch quantities in stock. Use the Post Goods Movements
app to post changes in material or changes in batches.
 Stock usability
Transfer postings that result in a change in stock usability involve a change in the
stock type. In general, most stock types can be transferred interchangeably. How-
ever, if quality management is active for a material in a plant, then transfers into or
out of quality inspection stock must be done in conjunction with a quality manage-
ment process, such as inbound inspection. Movement types used to transfer stock
from one stock type to another are shown in Table 7.1. Use the Transfer Stock—In-
Plant app for transfer postings from one stock type to another within a plant.
 Stock ownership
If you have stocks delivered to your facility by a supplier on a consignment basis and
you wish to take financial ownership of these stocks prior to consumption, you
enter a transfer posting to recognize that fact. Similarly, if you accept returns of
stock delivered on a consignment basis to your customer, you post a transfer post-
ing as well. Movement type 411 K is provided for this purpose. Use the Transfer
Stock—In-Plant app to post stock ownership changes within a plant.

The system provides a variety of physical inventory methods to accomplish this

A physical inventory document is required to start the process. This document forms

for posting any differences found between the system and the physical stocks. Physical
inventory documents contain a header, which holds information about the count
event itself, such as the document number, the person responsible for the count, and
the planned count date. Line items on the physical inventory document contain the
materials being counted and hold the system and actual count information. Stocks are
counted in inventory management based on the following:
 Material
 Plant

 Stock type
 Valuation type/batch
 Special stock

The method of creating physical inventory documents is dependent on the technique

 Manual physical inventory (spot inventory)
 Annual physical inventory
 Continuous physical inventory
 Cycle counting
 Sample-based physical inventory
For additional information on these physical inventory methods, consult the SAP Help
website.
Once the documents are created, it is common to print the physical inventory count
sheets. These are then distributed to the counters, who record the physical quantities on
the sheet. Count sheets can be transferred to a mobile application for counting as well.
After the physical count is recorded, this information is entered into the SAP S/4HANA
system. The system can provide feedback to the entry clerk if the quantity recorded
during the count exceeds the system count based on a defined threshold percentage.
This helps prevent data entry errors.
Once the counts are entered, they can be analyzed by authorized personnel. This anal-
ysis may result in a recount of the material in that storage location. Once the physical
inventory counts are confirmed, any differences detected need to be posted to inven-
tory management so that the physical and system counts are reconciled. This action
results in a goods movement posting either incrementing or decrementing the quan-
tity of goods in stock. Financial postings are also made at the same time.
SAP S/4HANA supplies apps to use in managing the physical inventory processes sup-
ported by the system. There are apps to support the execution of a physical inventory
and others for monitoring the physical inventory processes and reporting. SAP sup-
plies the following SAP Fiori apps to support physical inventory processes:

7.5 Reporting in Inventory Management
Proper control of physical stocks requires a robust set of reporting capabilities. S/4HANA
builds on SAP ERP’s inventory management reporting strengths by adding new capabili-
ties to visualize the current stock situation, thus enabling fast action in the case of logis-
tics bottlenecks. These capabilities include inventory analytics, which show key perfor-
mance indicators in real time, and the inventory overview pages, new in SAP S/4HANA,
which show multiple key analytics on a single screen.
There are a number of inventory management reporting apps that come delivered with
the SAP S/4HANA system. These apps can be broadly grouped into six types:
 Inventory overview pages
 Goods movements reporting apps
 Stock balances reporting apps
 Monitoring financial inventory values apps
 Inventory management object pages
 Inventory analytics
We’ll discuss each type in the sections that follow.

This app provides detailed information on materials that have turnover issues based

7.6 Configuring Inventory Management
Inventory management is a core supply chain capability of the SAP S/4HANA system.
Inventory management functions are delivered by SAP to work based on standard set-
tings. However, to realize the full features and functionalities of this component to
support an enterprise’s goals, the system does need to be fine-tuned based on business
requirements. This section details the standard SAP-recommended configuration steps
for inventory management. These settings are made in the SAP S/4HANA system by
following the customizing path provided in the following sections for each step.

7 Inventory Management
308
With SAP S/4HANA, it is possible to take advantage of the SAP Best Practices activation
approach for customizing, as explained in Chapter 2. However, if you use the tradi-
tional customizing approach, this section can help. This information also helps validate
the SAP standard configuration.
The following management configuration elements are described in the sections
ahead:
 General configuration elements
– Number Assignment assigns customer number ranges to inventory management
documents.
 Configuration elements for goods receipts and goods issues
– Set Expiration Date Check controls how expiration date checking is done in a
plant.
– Allow Negative Stocks controls whether negative stock balances are allowed and
in which storage locations.
 Configuration elements for movement types
– Record Reasons for Movement Types assigns specific codes to describe the pur-
pose of a goods movement.
– Copy, Change Movement Types allows the creation of new movement types.
 Configuration elements for stock transport purchase orders
– Define Shipping Data for Plants assigns the customer and sales area data needed
to process stock transport orders with delivery documents.
– Configure Delivery Type & Availability Check Procedure by Plant determines the
delivery document types used for intracompany and intercompany stock trans-
port orders for a plant.
– Assign Document Type, One-Step Procedure, Underdelivery Tolerance assigns the
proper outbound delivery document type for a specific plant pair. It also contains
settings to control one-step or two-step processing and tolerances for goods
receipt.
 Configuration elements for physical inventory
– Default Values for Physical Inventory sets the values that default into each physi-
cal inventory document.
– Settings for Physical Inventory sets additional values for the control of the physi-
cal inventory process for each plant.
– Allow Freezing of Book Inventory Balances in Storage Locations controls the freez-
ing behavior of book inventories during the physical inventory process.
– Cycle Counting sets specific controls for cycle counting per plant.

7.6.2 Goods Receipts and Goods Issues
Let’s take a look at the configuration elements for goods receipts and goods issues. In
this section, we’ll explore how to set expiration date checks and how to allow negative
stocks.
Set Expiration Date Check
SAP S/4HANA can check that a perishable item has sufficient shelf life remaining at the
time of goods receipt. To do this, a minimum remaining shelf life has to be maintained
in the material master record. In addition, the ability to check shelf life for each plant
and movement type has to be maintained in configuration. These checks are not
enabled in the standard SAP S/4HANA system.
The menu path to enable shelf life expiration date checks is IMG (SPRO)  Materials
Management  Inventory Management and Physical Inventory  Goods Receipt  Set
Expiration Date Check. The Activate/Deactivate Expiration Date Check screen appears
(see Figure 7.64).

7.6.3 Movement Types
Let’s take a look at movement types and their configuration elements. In this section,
we’ll discuss recording reasons for movement types and how to copy and change
movement types.
Record Reasons for Movement Types
It’s possible to have the system record a reason for a goods movement at the time of
posting. For example, you can require a reason to be entered when a goods issue to
scrapping is performed. With this configuration item, you can require the entry of a
reason for a specific movement type and also maintain the valid reasons that can be
selected.
To make these settings, navigate to IMG (SPRO)  Materials Management  Inventory
Management and Physical Inventory  Movement Types  Record Reasons for Movement
Types. The Reason for Movement screen appears (see Figure 7.70).

Copy, Change Movement Types
SAP S/4HANA comes with many movement types, which handle nearly every business
inventory transaction. However, it can be desirable to set up new movement types to
handle specific situations in your enterprise. For instance, you may want new move-
ment types to handle a goods issue for consumption to support research and develop-
ment. SAP S/4HANA allows you to create new movement types to support your
enterprise’s requirements.
There are three rules to follow when creating new movement types:
1. Always copy an existing movement type that is similar to the type of movement you
are creating. For example, if you’re creating a new goods issue movement type, copy

an existing goods issue movement type. Copy all dependent entries, as there is a
large amount of integration of inventory management with other areas of SAP
S/4HANA, such as finance and quality management. Don’t attempt to create a move-
ment type from scratch!
2. Always copy the copied movement type’s reversal movement type as well. All move-
ment types require a reversal movement.
3. There are ranges of codes that SAP sets aside for customer-created movement types.
Most SAP S/4HANA customers create new movement types that start with Y, Z, or 9.

7.6.4 Stock Transport Orders
Let’s examine the configuration elements needed to set up stock transport orders in

 Set delivery type and availability checking per purchasing document type and sup-
plying plant
 Set delivery types and set the one-step/two-step process for each plant pair, needed
to determine the proper scenario (intracompany or intercompany) and the process
by which goods receipts are performed (automatic or manual)
Define Shipping Data for Plants

7.6.5 Physical Inventory
Now let’s take a look at the configuration elements for physical inventory. Here you’ll
see how to configure default values, settings, freezing balances, and cycle counting.
Default Values for Physical Inventory
This configuration item allows you to set the default values used in the physical inven-
tory processes for each plant. Settings are established that default into each physical
inventory document created in that plant.
To review default values for physical inventory, navigate to IMG (SPRO)  Materials
Management  Inventory Management and Physical Inventory  Physical Inventory 
Default Values for Physical Inventory. The Physical Inventory Settings screen appears
(see Figure 7.82). Click the checkbox next to the plant for which you want to maintain
default values, then click the Details button.
The Physical Inventory Settings screen appears (see Figure 7.83). Determine the default
stock type for the documents (1 is unrestricted stock). Click the Batch in Background
checkbox for the batches in inventory to be predetermined and copied to the physical
inventory document being created. Click the Alternative Unit of Measure checkbox if
you want to be able to record counts in alternative units of measure. You can also main-
tain a default reason for inventory differences if desired. Press the Save button.

Allow Freezing of Book Inventory Balances in Storage Locations
This configuration item allows you to determine if freezing of book inventories will be
done when physical inventory documents are activated. If book inventories are frozen,
inventory differences found during the count will be calculated from the frozen stock
balance. If book inventories are not frozen, then inventory differences will be calcu-
lated from the stock balance at the time the count is recorded. This indicator can be set
at the storage location level.
To allow freezing of book inventory balances in storage locations, navigate to IMG

This configuration item allows you to make necessary settings for using the cycle

sections.title: Summary
sections.text:
7.7 Summary
You now know that SAP S/4HANA provides a comprehensive app portfolio for record-
ing the receipt, placement, and issue of goods in your facilities. There are many apps
that allow you to report the impacts of those goods movements at a tactical and a stra-
tegic level. You can also assess the impacts of those goods movements on the logistics
supply chain and on the financials of your company.
The next chapter of this book will explore contract and scheduling agreement manage-
ment, which is one of the key concepts used in SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and Procure-
ment for securing and administering long-term supply arrangements for your
company.
